 2026 Midterm Elections Election Day live blog: Updates on federal monitors and problems at the polls
 Voters are heading to the polls amid unprecedented concern about federal interference. Votebeat will live-blog every development.
 By  Natalia Contreras , Hayley Harding , Sasha Hupka , Dion Nissenbaum , Alexander Shur , Carter Walker , Tia Yang , Lauren Aguirre , Elaine Cromie , Sami Edge , Jessica Huseman , Carrie Levine and Nathaniel Rakich  |  November 3, 2026, 11:00am UTC 
 Republish lead-art-block.fullscreen-enter Expand Voters wait in line to cast their ballot at the Indian Bend Wash Visitors Center in Scottsdale, Arizona. (Ash Ponders for Votebeat) Votebeat is a nonprofit news organization reporting on voting access and election administration across the U.S. Sign up for our free weekly newsletter to get the latest. 
 It’s finally Election Day 2026, and voters across the country are heading to the polls. Will they face any obstacles there? The specter of federal interference has loomed large over these midterms as President Donald Trump has sought to change the way states run elections. And we’ve already seen some more typical problems crop up, including issues scanning ballots in Westchester County, New York, and a record-keeping error in Milwaukee. 
 Follow Votebeat’s Election Day live blog below as our reporters bring you live updates on how voting is unfolding across the country.

 Election Day live blog: Updates on federal monitors and problems at the polls Voters are heading to the polls amid unprecedented concern about federal interference.
 By  Natalia Contreras , Hayley Harding and 11 more  |  Today, 11:00am UTC Everything you need to know about post-election audits Officials in all 50 states conduct post-election audits to verify that election results are accurate and procedures were followed properly.
 By  Carter Walker  |  Today, 10:00am UTC Alaska has a two-Dan problem in key Senate race. But voter confusion seems unlikely to matter. Alaska’s unusual ranked choice voting process makes it less likely confusion over two Dans will matter in a key Senate race.
 By  Dion Nissenbaum  |  November 2 La renovada ley electoral de Texas ha limitado la ayuda a algunos de los ciudadanos más vulnerables del estado. Los grupos han modificado o detenido sus esfuerzos de difusión entre los votantes, preocupados por las sanciones penales.
 By  Natalia Contreras and traduccion por Flavia Franco  |  November 2 When to expect midterm results in Arizona The first batch of election results will drop around 8 p.m., but full results typically take days.
 By  Sasha Hupka  |  November 2 Mail voting plummeted in a Nebraska county targeted by election fraud activists The Nebraska Voter Accuracy Project claims credit for a drop in mail voting in Sarpy County. An investigation found no fraud, and voting data cannot establish what caused the decline.
